questions.question: If you see hazardous materials leaking while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Park the vehicle as soon as possible.
Leave the area to find help.
Drive around looking for someone to fix the leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: If hazardous materials start leaking, stop driving right away. The longer you drive, the larger the spill becomes. Park the vehicle, secure the area, and stay with it while someone else gets help.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for hazardous chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
questions.explanation: The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) Emergency Response Guide lists hazardous materials by shipping names and identification numbers.

questions.question: Which type of tank has the strongest surge?
questions.explanation: Unbaffled tanks have no internal walls to stop the liquid from moving. They are the most prone to surge.

questions.question: Because tank vehicles have high centers of gravity, drivers should:

options.text: Take curves at the posted speed limit.
Drive on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Tank vehicles can easily tip over because of their high centers of gravity. Always drive slowly through curves.

questions.question: What should be done with wheel rims that have been welded?

options.text: Place them in the front of the vehicle.
Place them in the rear of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Wheels and rims with welding repairs are not safe. Replace any damaged wheels and rims.

questions.question: What can a hand valve be used for?

options.text: Keep a truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops the vehicle from rolling backward when you start from a stop.

questions.question: What do smooth bore tanks have inside?

options.text: Bulkheads with holes for liquid to pass through.

questions.explanation: Smooth bore tanks have no internal baffles. This makes them the most likely to have front-to-back surge.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness before a trip?

options.text: Get about four hours of sleep.
Plan stopping points into your trip in advance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan stopping points into your trip in advance.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, get enough sleep before you drive, plan your route and stops ahead of time, drive with a passenger, and drive during times when you are normally awake.

questions.question: How far ahead should you scan the road?
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to spot hazards and react before you reach them. Look for vehicles entering the highway, changing lanes, or turning.

questions.question: When using road speed to decide when to shift gears, you should:

options.text: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
Watch other vehicles and match their speed.
Watch other trucks and shift when they do.
Use the speed limit as a guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift: engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Read your vehicle's manual to learn which speeds work for each gear. Watch your speedometer and shift up as needed.

questions.question: When changing lanes, your turn signal:

options.text: Should only be used if other vehicles are present.
Should only be used at night.

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: If an explosives package has an oily stain or is damp, the driver should:
questions.explanation: Never transport damaged explosives packages. Refuse any package that appears damp or has an oily stain.

questions.question: Emergency response information from the shipper must include:
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include basic descriptions and technical names of materials; health hazards; fire and explosion risks; what to do in case of an accident; how to handle fires; how to handle spills or leaks; and first aid steps.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is thin and clear. You can see the road through it, so it looks like wet pavement.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Rely on your mirrors to guide you.
Walk around first to check for obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing, walk around your vehicle to check the path and look for obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so do not rely on them alone. Use a helper when possible.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when you use them, it means:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, you have a brake problem. Fix it before driving. Unsafe vehicles break federal and state laws.

questions.question: When driving, knowing what is behind you is:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires knowing what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Use your mirrors often.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Watch the road for hazards. Plan how you would handle them if they become emergencies.

questions.question: When approaching a bridge or overpass, you should:

options.text: Trust that the posted clearance height is correct.
Assume the posted clearance height may be wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the posted clearance height may be wrong.
questions.explanation: Do not trust posted height clearances. Road repaving or packed snow can change the actual height. If you are unsure your vehicle will fit, slow down and find another route.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, turning toward the driver's side is encouraged:

options.text: Because it gives the driver a better view.
Because turning toward the passenger side is illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because it gives the driver a better view.
questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view of where your vehicle is going.
